learningObjective: Diagnose overflow in FP16 accumulation on a long reduction and explain why FP32 accumulation is required.

canonicalClaims.claim: FP16's maximum representable magnitude (~65504) is easily exceeded by long reductions of moderate-magnitude partial products; FP32 accumulation is required to keep intermediate sums in range, with the final result downcast to FP16 on write.
conditions: K is large enough (roughly K ≥ 1024 for typical DNN magnitudes) to risk overflow.
Input distribution has non-negligible mass in the moderate-magnitude regime.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP16 accumulation is always dangerous — small-K or bounded-input reductions can be safe.
Does not imply BF16 removes all overflow risk downstream (e.g., squaring can still overflow).

misconceptions.whyWrong: Precision (mantissa width) and dynamic range (exponent width) are orthogonal; FP32 has both larger, but the range difference is what prevents overflow here.

misconceptions.claim: FP16 GEMM is broken in principle; only FP32 GEMM produces meaningful results.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP16 GEMM with FP32 accumulation is a standard, well-tested configuration used across cuBLAS Tensor Core kernels.

misconceptions.claim: Only very large K (K > 10^6) can cause FP16 accumulation to overflow.
misconceptions.whyWrong: K on the order of 10^3 with unit-magnitude inputs is already at risk; typical GEMMs in Transformers have K = 4096 or more.

misconceptions.claim: Downcasting the FP32 accumulator to FP16 on the final write reintroduces the same overflow.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The overflow happens during accumulation, not at the final write; if the final result fits in FP16, downcast is safe (else it produces INF at write, one value at a time).

implementationFacts: cuBLAS FP16 Tensor Core GEMM uses FP32 accumulator by default.
PyTorch autocast for FP16 uses FP32 for reductions and BN stats.
performanceScenarios: Transformer FFN layer with hidden_dim=4096 exhibits partial-sum magnitudes >65504 with typical input distributions.
